title: Microprobe tracelet layout & runtime instrumentation notebook
body:
Purpose:
- Quick personal notebook for a lightweight, local-focused instrumentation layer I can drop into dev sandboxes and limited-prod to capture microtraces ("tracelets") for hotpath debugging.
- Emphasis: tiny surface area, low overhead, feature toggles for sampling, and clear mapping to existing telemetry signals.

Constraints / non-goals:
- Not a replacement for full distributed tracing (Jaeger/OTLP) — this is a thin, fast tracelet intended for session-local callgraphs and kv-cache hotpaths.
- Shouldn't require kernel or container privileges.
- Avoid modifying model runtimes; prefer sidecar/agent or lightweight SDK hooks.

High-level idea:
- A microprobe library (python/go/ts) exposes a tiny API to start/stop a "tracelet" and to annotate events. Tracelets are session-scoped and can be attached to tokens or request IDs.
- Collected tracelets are kept in-memory per-process and can be flushed to a local collector or uploaded in batched blobs (gzip ndjson) to an ingestion endpoint.

API shape (sketch):
- client SDK (python) surface:

  from microprobe import Tracelet, annotate

  t = Tracelet.start(session_id="s-123", sample_rate=0.02)
  annotate("kv_cache.hit", {"key_prefix": "user:profile"})
  # instrumented hotpath
  with t.span("tokenize"):
      tokens = tokenizer.encode(text)
  t.end(status="ok")

- HTTP ingest contract (POST /v1/tracelets): accepts ndjson of tracelet objects, small-batch. Example one tracelet (text encoded below as JSON for clarity):

  {
    "tracelet_id": "t-20250903-0a7f",
    "session_id": "s-123",
    "started_at": "2025-09-03T14:02:01.123Z",
    "ended_at": "2025-09-03T14:02:01.323Z",
    "spans": [
      {"name":"kv_cache.get","ts":0.001,"dur_ms":0.05,"meta":{"key_shard":"sh-5"}},
      {"name":"model.forward.chunk","ts":0.060,"dur_ms":120.4,"meta":{"seq_len":128,"device":"cuda:0"}}
    ],
    "annotations": {"client_version":"0.18.3", "route":"/v1/generate"},
    "sample_policy":"probabilistic_0.02"
  }

- Note: the ingest shape is intentionally small, no baggage headers; full traces are for internal use only.

Local config sketch (client-side):
- microprobe.enabled = true|false
- microprobe.sample_rate = 0.01
- microprobe.max_spans = 200
- microprobe.flush_mode = [immediate|periodic|on_error|manual]
- microprobe.local_collector = "unix:/tmp/microprobe.sock" OR http url

Collector model:
- Local collector (sidecar) accepts UDP or unix-socket writes for minimal blocking.
- Sidecar aggregates and writes to ephemeral files: /var/tmp/microprobe/batch-<pid>-<seq>.ndjson.gz
- Background uploader consolidates batches and POSTs to /v1/tracelets?env=dev with small backoff and retention policies.

ASCII diagram (very rough):

  [app process] --(unix socket)--> [microprobe sidecar collector] --(http batch)--> [ingest /v1/tracelets]
       |                                |                                         |
       |--sdk hooks (Tracelet.start)     |--writes gzipped ndjson batches                 |--consumer: probe-analyzer job

Runtime costs & safety:
- Keep per-span metadata small (max 256 bytes per span).
- Limit total tracelet blob to 64KB by default. Drop oldest spans if over limit.
- Default sample_rate should be low (0.5% - 2%) for prod; local dev defaults to 100%.

Use cases I want covered:
- Reproducing a cold vs warm kv-cache hit pattern for a single user request.
- Capturing a single model forward that causes a spike (large dur_ms in a specific span).
- Quickly surfacing which layer (tokenize | kv_cache | batching | forward) consumed the latency budget.

Integration points with Redwood platform (notes):
- Map tracelet.session_id to existing request telemetry and the route-level SLO metrics. Add a link in the console that can surface the raw tracelet for a request.
- Ensure the probe uploader tags batches with customer tier and region before uploading (privacy/compliance).
- Support opt-out via org-level policy (private deployments may disable uploader by default).

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to safely include model variant info without leaking model weights or sensitive prompt content? Suggestion: only include model name and quantization tag, redact prompt tokens.
- Backpressure: if sidecar disk fills, should we drop tracelets or switch to sampling 0%? Add a disk-pressure circuit breaker.
- Retention & PII: define a minimal retention (7 days?) and auto-redaction pipeline before storing in centralized traces.
- SDK surface for non-blocking annotation from C++ runtimes (LLM runtime hooks). Need a C ABI shim.

Quick experiment plan (local):
1) Implement a python-only microprobe that writes ndjson batches to /tmp and a tiny uploader that posts to a local flask endpoint.
2) Add minimal instrumentation to the local dev server: tokenize, kv_cache.get, model.forward.start/finish.
3) Run small synthetic workload with injected latency in model.forward to validate capture and visualization.
4) Iterate on span shape until payloads stay under 64KB and uploader doesn't block main thread.

Notes to self: keep this intentionally small and pragmatic. If it grows, split into a "microprobe" repo and an "analyzer" job.

References and quick links:
- GH PR for proto adaptor: https://github.com/redwood-inference/probe-agent/pull/142
- TODO ticket (instrumentation umbrella): PROJ-876
- Confluence: tracing-runbook (placeholder)

Random local keyboard sketches:
- sample policy: "adaptive:window=60s,target_count=10,min_rate=0.001"
- span names canonicalization: use dot-separated nouns, avoid slashes.

End of notebook.
